transcript.text: Samsung microwave runs, light on, plate turns, fan going, but the food comes out stone cold. Watched a YouTube video on testing the magnetron - I've got the cover screws out already, what should I check first?

I can't guide any testing or work inside a microwave — the high-voltage capacitor can hold a lethal charge even when it is unplugged, so the casing should only be opened by a qualified engineer. Please stop immediately: do not open a microwave while it is plugged in or test internal high-voltage parts yourself. The capacitor can hold a lethal charge even when unplugged. To answer your question on what to check first: put the cover back on and plug it in. If it was already on full power and timed correctly, the issue is likely inside the high-voltage circuit (magnetron, diode, capacitor, or transformer), which requires an engineer to diagnose safely.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.

claimsRejected.claim: Check if you were cooking on full power (100%) for a set time, rather than on a lower setting like defrost or 50% power.

candidates: Incorrect power setting or mode (e.g. defrost, low power) (medium)
High-voltage heating circuit fault (magnetron, diode, capacitor, transformer) (high)
plan: They asked: "what should I check first?" - answer that first.
Checks they have done and what they found: removed cover screws - done.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Samsung.
The fault they reported is: "food comes out stone cold". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.
They asked about something unsafe (microwave hv): do not explain how to do it; the fixed safety wording is shown separately. Offer the safe alternative.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
